the quality of ANC in Vietnam should be improved in both the public and the private sector, and that the private sector should be regulated to improve quality of services.
the ANC services in Vietnam are not sufficient to meet the needs of women, especially the poor and the rural ones, as related to the WHO and the national recommendations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of factors, including demographic, social and health system factors, is associated with inadequate ANC use in both rural and urban areas of Vietnam.
the quality of ANC in Vietnam is low, particularly in the rural areas and that there is an urgent need to improve the quality of ANC.
ANC is not a simple intervention, but a complex one, with many interacting factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of ANC in Vietnam needs to be improved, especially in the rural areas.
the private sector is not a panacea for the provision of ANC.
ANC in Vietnam needs to be improved in order to meet national recommendations and to be effective in reducing the risk of poor maternal and infant outcomes.
